messages:
maria: quick update — finished a focused KV-cache quantization run across FP8-KV vs INT8-KV and a small GPTQ/AWQ pass. wanted to share summary and ask for ideas on two odd tail cases.

alex: nice. what model / seq len / batch did you use?

maria: model=tiny-redwood-6B (bringup test), context=8k, perf window=1M tokens, batch=1/2 for latency probes. kv quantization: FP8-KV (per-tensor scale, e4m2-like FP8 emulation), INT8-KV (symmetric per-channel), GPTQ stripped baseline and a small AWQ run.

maria: config snippet:
```
model: tiny-redwood-6B
context: 8192
kv_quant: 
  fp8_kv: {type: emu_e4m2, per_tensor_scale: true}
  int8_kv: {type: per_channel_symmetric}
batch_sizes: [1,2]
seq_lengths: [128,1024,4096,8192]
metrics: [latency_p50,p95,p99,mem_bytes,accuracy_delta]
```

bench-bot: results pasted below (median of 3 runs):
```
FP8-KV  | mem -27.6% | p50 12.8ms | p95 25.9ms | p99 54.2ms | acc_delta vs fp32: -0.6%
INT8-KV | mem -19.1% | p50 14.5ms | p95 31.2ms | p99 120ms  | acc_delta vs fp32: -0.2%
GPTQ-KV | mem -33.1% | p50 13.9ms | p95 40.1ms | p99 210ms  | acc_delta vs fp32: -1.8%
AWQ-KV  | mem -31.0% | p50 13.4ms | p95 35.5ms | p99 160ms  | acc_delta vs fp32: -1.1%
```

jin: interesting — FP8-KV gives best p50/p95 and big mem win. but p99 for INT8 is much worse than FP8? looks like dequant penalty on cache miss path. did you isolate warm vs cold KV cache?

maria: yeah we split warm/cold. warm (after 5k tokens) FP8 p99 ~48ms, INT8 p99 ~47ms. the big INT8 p99 spike happens at cold starts in long context workloads (first few continuations) — likely extra dequant ops in critical path for per-channel int8.

sam: do we have CPU-side dequant cost breakdown? maybe INT8 dequant is multithreaded and contends with async IO causing tail spikes.

maria: added flame trace snippet (truncated):
```
thread0: kv_lookup -> memcpy -> dequant_int8_per_channel -> apply_attn -> writeback
thread0: kv_lookup -> memcpy -> fp8_dequant_fastpath -> apply_attn -> writeback
```

ops-bot: note: dedicated test workers used gpu-node-9 (A800-like), 32GB HBM, driver 525.

jin: do we trust FP8 accuracy numbers? -0.6% avg seems okay but could hide long-tail token errors. which eval sets?

maria: eval sets = code + longform summarization + chat-like completions (mix). accuracy_delta is composite BLEU/ROUGE/LM-logprob normalized. breakdown: code:-0.3, summarization:-0.9, chat:-0.7 (FP8 slightly worse on hallucination markers in chat).

sam: possible plan: 1) add per-layer FP8 fallback for top-k layers (reduce hallucinations), 2) rerun INT8 with fused dequant kernel (we have a prototype), 3) AWQ/GPTQ verify on longer finetune checkpoints.

alex: how big is memory regression at batch=2? we plan Dedicated footprints.

maria: batch=2 mem numbers: FP8 -25%, INT8 -16%, GPTQ -30% (kV storage dominated). For Dedicated planning FP8 gives best density.

bench-bot: added CSV export link: https://bench.internal/runs/1779004321/csv (results+raw traces) :card_file_box:

jin: can someone reproduce with prefetch disabled? that was a confounder in earlier runs.

maria: good call — will rerun with prefetch=false and fused-int8 kernels enabled. scheduling for tomorrow AM.

sam: also add a small prompt-eval that stresses hallucination tokens and measure per-token logprob drift across quant variants.

alex: assign @maria to follow up and @jin to own kernel test.

maria: got it — I'll post updated run (prefetch off + fused-int8) and add per-layer FP8 fallback experiment results. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: created ticket REDWOOD-ml/INFER-872 for follow-up experiments (assignee: maria).
